sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia. Ladakh (alias Leh / Leh-Ladakh) is at 3524m. Acclimatisation of 24–48 hours recommended before exertion. Most roads, passes and monasteries are seasonal (May–Sep). All records needs_review.

places.name: Leh Palace
places.description: Nine-storey royal palace built in the 17th century by King Sengge Namgyal, modelled on the Potala Palace in Lhasa. Now a partly ruined but intact shell managed by ASI; good views over Leh bazaar and the valley. The climb from the old city is steep on uneven lanes. Budget 1 hour. The adjacent Namgyal Tsemo Gompa is a further 15-min steep walk above.

places.name: Shanti Stupa
places.description: White-domed Buddhist stupa built in 1991 on a hilltop in the Chanspa neighbourhood, a gift from Japanese Buddhist organisations. 340 steps from the road or driveable by taxi. Panoramic views over Leh valley at sunrise and sunset. Free entry; a short meditation garden at the top.

places.name: Hemis Monastery
places.description: Ladakh's largest, wealthiest and most visited monastery, 45km south of Leh in the Hemis National Park gorge. Founded in 1630, belonging to the Drukpa Kagyu school. Houses a famous thangka (embroidery) of Padmasambhava that is displayed every 12 years (next: 2029). The Hemis Festival (two-day masked Cham dance) takes place in June or July annually and draws large crowds.

places.name: Thiksey Monastery
places.description: 12-storey monastery complex built on a conic hill 17km east of Leh, resembling the Potala Palace in scale. Houses around 500 monks of the Gelug school; contains a 15m Maitreya Buddha statue in the main hall. The climb from the parking area is substantial. Morning puja begins at 06:00 — peaceful and photogenic. Often combined with Hemis on a southern circuit day.

places.name: Namgyal Tsemo Gompa
places.description: 15th-century Buddhist monastery atop the peak behind Leh Palace, containing a three-storey statue of Maitreya and 500-year-old manuscripts. The steep climb from the old city is demanding at altitude; rewards with the best panoramic views over Leh. Best visited very early morning or evening for light. The trail passes through the old town's narrow lanes.

places.name: Magnetic Hill
places.description: A roadside optical illusion on the Leh–Kargil highway, 30km northwest of Leh, where the road gradient and surrounding terrain make stationary vehicles appear to roll uphill. Widely described as anti-gravity but is a well-documented hill illusion. A 10-minute stop; typically combined with Gurudwara Pathar Sahib and the Indus-Zanskar confluence when driving the Srinagar-Leh highway.
places.openingDays: Open all day (May–Oct; road may close in winter)

places.name: Khardung La Pass
places.description: High mountain pass at 5359m altitude, 38km north of Leh on the road to Nubra Valley. The road is maintained by BRO and is one of the highest motorable roads in the world. A brief stop at the top (tea stalls, signboards) before descending to Nubra; vehicle permit from Leh mandatory. Road condition varies; typically open Jun–Sep, sometimes closed by snowfall even in summer.

places.name: Spituk Monastery
places.description: Gelug school monastery built in the 11th century on a conical hill at the edge of the Indus plain, 8km from Leh near Kushok Bakula Airport. Three tiers of chortens and prayer halls ascend the hill; the top shrine contains an idol of Mahakala whose face is only revealed during the annual Spituk Gustor festival (January). Good views of the Indus valley.

places.name: Hall of Fame Museum
places.description: Indian Army museum in Leh commemorating soldiers who served in the Siachen Glacier conflict and the Kargil War. Houses weapons, uniforms, letters, photographs and a scale model of the glacier. Well maintained; sobering and informative account of high-altitude warfare in Ladakh's strategic corridors. A 1-hour visit.

places.name: Leh Main Bazaar
places.description: The central market of Leh town, running along Main Bazaar Road from the Jama Masjid to the Polo Ground. Shops sell Ladakhi and Tibetan crafts (thangkas, carpets, pashmina, prayer flags), trekking gear, and dried apricots. The bazaar atmosphere reflects Ladakh's intersection of Tibetan Buddhist and Central Asian trading cultures. Best explored on foot in the morning.

places.name: Stok Palace
places.description: Palace of the royal family of Ladakh (Namgyal dynasty), 15km south of Leh. Built in the 1820s when the Dogra army captured Leh; the royal family was moved here from Leh Palace. One wing houses a museum of royal regalia, thangkas and a crown with a 45-carat emerald. Still partly inhabited by the royal family. Often combined with Hemis and Thiksey on the southern monastery circuit.

places.name: Alchi Monastery
places.description: 11th-century monastery complex in the Indus Valley, 70km west of Leh, containing some of the oldest and most important surviving Buddhist murals and wood sculpture in Ladakh. Unique because it sits on flat ground (not a hilltop) in a village setting. The Dukhang and Sum-Tsek temples are among the finest examples of Kashmir-influenced Buddhist art. Combines well with Likir and Basgo on the western circuit.

places.name: Likir Monastery
places.description: Gelug school monastery founded in the 11th century on a ridge above the Indus Valley, 52km west of Leh. Notable for a 23m gold-painted Maitreya Buddha statue visible from the road. The monastery museum holds a significant collection of Tibetan artefacts and thangkas. Quieter than Thiksey or Hemis; often combined with Alchi and Basgo on a western circuit day trip.

places.name: Lamayuru Monastery
places.description: Possibly Ladakh's oldest monastery (11th century), dramatically sited on a hilltop above a 'moonland' terrain of eroded clay pinnacles, 127km west of Leh. The surrounding landscape is among the most photographed in India. Belongs to the Drikung Kagyu school. The Yuru Kabgyat festival (Cham dance) takes place in late June/July. A worthwhile half-day from Leh or a stop on the Srinagar–Leh drive.

places.name: Gurudwara Pathar Sahib
places.description: Sikh gurudwara 25km northwest of Leh on the Srinagar-Leh highway, commemorating Guru Nanak's visit to Ladakh and his encounter with a local demon as described in Sikh hagiography. Built and maintained by the Indian Army. Free langar (community meal) served to all visitors; open to all faiths. Typically combined with Magnetic Hill and the Indus-Zanskar confluence on a highway excursion.

places.name: Indus–Zanskar Confluence
places.description: Point near Nimmu village, 37km west of Leh, where the turquoise Zanskar River meets the grey-green Indus. The colour contrast is visually striking and well-known as a photography subject. Viewpoint accessible directly from the roadside on the Srinagar–Leh highway. A brief 15-minute stop on the western highway circuit; typically combined with Magnetic Hill and Gurudwara Pathar Sahib.

places.name: Chang La Pass
places.description: Mountain pass at 5360m altitude on the Leh–Pangong Lake road, 47km southeast of Leh. The third-highest motorable pass in the world. A mandatory crossing on the Pangong Lake route; a BRO post and tea stalls at the top. The pass itself takes 20–30 min; altitude acclimatisation before crossing is important. Combined with Pangong Lake as a full-day or overnight trip from Leh.
places.area: 47km SE of Leh, en route to Pangong
places.openingDays: May–Oct (weather dependent; frequently blocked by snow even in summer)

places.name: Basgo Palace
places.description: Ruined 15th-century palace complex on a hilltop at Basgo village, 40km west of Leh. Once the capital of lower Ladakh, the ruins include a citadel, granary and two temples (Chamba Lhakhang, Serzang Lhakhang) with well-preserved wooden carvings and ancient murals. Requires a climb through the ruins. Best combined with Alchi and Likir on the western circuit. Free entry.

places.name: Phyang Monastery
places.description: Drikung Kagyu monastery perched above Phyang village, 16km northwest of Leh. Founded in the 16th century, it houses around 70 monks and contains significant Ladakhi artefacts and thangkas. The bi-annual Phyang Tsedup festival (Cham dance with Thangka procession) takes place in July. Less visited than Thiksey or Hemis; a quieter monastery experience.

places.name: Stakna Monastery
places.description: Small but picturesquely situated Drikung Kagyu monastery on a craggy hilltop above the Indus River, 25km south of Leh. Only about 30 monks; provides a genuine, uncrowded monastery experience. Excellent views of the river valley and the Stok Kangri mountain range. Often passed without stopping on the Leh–Hemis road; worth 45 minutes.

places.name: Ladakhi Thukpa and Skyu
places.description: Traditional Ladakhi cuisine at Leh Old Town dhabas: thukpa (hearty noodle broth with vegetables or meat), skyu (thick hand-rolled pasta with root vegetables), and tsampa (roasted barley flour porridge). Tibetan flatbread tingmo goes with almost everything. Warming and high-altitude appropriate.

places.name: Leh Market Café and Butter Tea
places.description: Leh Main Bazaar cafés offer butter tea (pos cha — salted yak butter tea), chhang (barley beer), and fresh apricot juice — all local to Ladakh. The apricot orchards of Ladakh produce juice and jam of extraordinary quality. A chance to try hyperlocal Himalayan beverages.
